meta.title: Contact and visitation chronology — recorded NRE and dates to review
meta.description: Since the 2017 judgment, reported contact requests and complaints in France, Norway and Germany: a personal account, contact calendar and legal sources.

reference.heading: Complaints filed since 2017 — France, Norway, Germany
reference.prefix: Since the judgment of 31 March 2017, I have filed complaints in France, Norway and Germany. These steps form part of years of attempts to maintain contact with my daughter.
reference.filed: A French complaint document appears below. Filing a complaint does not establish an outcome in any jurisdiction.

note.heading: Why I am making these efforts visible
note.p1: I am publishing this history to show my repeated attempts to see my daughter. In my account, our separation does not reflect a lack of interest or a decision to give up my responsibilities as a father.
note.p2: I have filed complaints and approached authorities in several countries over many years. Yet I consider that the available mechanisms did not secure regular contact or effectively protect our family relationship.
note.p3: I want to show the difference between having the right to make requests, filing a complaint, and actually being able to participate in a child’s life. These views are my own; judicial facts must be assessed against the decisions and records.
note.expand: Read the rest of my account

timeline.heading: Timeline by year
timeline.lead: Each year shows first weekends of the month. ✗ = recorded historical NRE claim, ✓ = honored or partial, ? = unverified date. Later dates are not automatically criminal findings.
timeline.empty: No weekend matches the selected filters.

location.heading: Location
location.body: 2015 France; since 2017 Norway, Oslo; since 2022 Germany, Frankfurt.

table.heading: First weekends of each month
table.lead: Historic inventory is published through February 2026. From March 2026, dates are generated automatically but their status requires checking the reported German court decision.

exceptions.heading: Reported honored or partial visits
exceptions.lead: Six contact periods are listed in the archives: some involve longer stays, others brief meetings. Holiday dates still need reconciling with the documents.
exceptions.genericDetail: Reported brief meeting: approximately one hour.
exceptions.extendedStay: Longer stay reported; do not add an extra hour on top of holiday time without checking overlaps.
exceptions.otherWeekend: Reported visit: date not yet matched to the separately reported 24-hour weekend.

hours.heading: Time together — estimate from reported periods
hours.net: Elapsed time minus the estimated subtotal of stays
hours.scope: In France, two stays of 7 days and one of 28 days are converted to 24 hours per day of presence; exact dates are not yet matched to the calendar.
hours.source: In Germany, a meeting of around 1 h and a later weekend of about 24 h are reported. In Norway, about three one-hour meetings are reported; their dates remain unknown, so they are included only once in the overall estimate, not assigned to calendar cards.
hours.refresh: The timer updates each second. The month inventory is recalculated from the local Paris date.
hours.suspension: A German contact suspension was reported from 26 February 2026 through 25 February 2027; the operative court order has not been verified here. Later dates are not labeled NRE.
hours.beforeOrder: The March 2017 row predates the cited 31 March 2017 decision and needs review.
hours.intro: According to my account, the scheduled 10 hours per weekend were never respected; rare meetings lasted around one hour.
hours.netHint: Indicative and incomplete: the 42 French holiday days count calendar co-presence, not directly measured contact. Three undated Norwegian meetings are included.
hours.methodology: Calculation method and overlaps to review
hours.contactEstimateHint: France: 42 holiday days counted as 24 h per calendar day (1,008 h). Germany: an approximately 1 h reunion and a 24 h weekend (25 h). Norway: approximately three one-hour meetings (3 h), with dates not yet identified.

advocacy.heading: I never stopped asking to see my daughter.
advocacy.lead: Since the judgment of 31 March 2017, I have continued requesting contact and pursuing remedies for years. I have filed complaints in France, Norway and Germany. Despite those efforts, I have not been able to build a regular relationship with my daughter.
advocacy.emphasis: Filing complaints is not the same as raising a child. My efforts show that I never stopped trying.
advocacy.countriesLabel: Three countries where complaints are reported
advocacy.stepsLabel: Years of efforts to preserve family contact
advocacy.requestBody: Keep seeking meetings and attempting to exercise contact rights despite the reported obstacles.
advocacy.complaintsBody: File complaints in France, Norway and Germany since the 2017 judgment, without assuming that each complaint led to the same outcome.
advocacy.consequenceTitle: Remain unable to share everyday life
advocacy.consequenceBody: According to my account, meetings remained rare and the remedies pursued did not secure a regular parent-child relationship.
advocacy.opinion: In my view, the authorities I contacted did not provide effective protection of our family life. This experience raises questions for me about the rule of law and the protection of fathers’ rights. This is my personal assessment, not a judicial finding against all states.
advocacy.evidenceNotice: This account describes reported actions and contact. Filing a complaint does not establish the alleged offence or the outcome of a case; dates and documents must be checked against available records.
advocacy.rightsIntro: The right to respect for family life is protected in particular by
advocacy.rightsLink: Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights

access.heading: Request access to a document or evidence
access.intro: This guide covers documents linked throughout Bababou, including central authority archives and evidence referenced in the NRE register. Private copies require individual disclosure approval.
access.pending: Protected access is being prepared. No private portal or download is available here.
access.step1Body: Use a public reference below and explain your role and purpose without uploading sensitive family information to this site.
access.step2Body: Once the private portal is activated, Cloudflare Access will verify identity and require an additional authentication factor. A public link does not authorize access.
access.step3Body: Cloudflare Access will ask for a justification and send the request to an authorized approver, who may accept or deny it. Any approved session will be time-limited.
access.step4Body: The private gateway will check permissions for each reference and deliver only an approved redacted copy. Access can be revoked and consultations will be logged.

access.securityBody: Originals, Docling extracts and OpenRAG indexes remain outside the public website. MFA or temporary approval does not authorize access to the entire file: each document needs a separate grant.
access.existingPublicPdf: A French complaint already exists among the website's older public files. That earlier publication must be audited separately; a future private gateway cannot retroactively protect it.
access.noAutomaticApproval: This website cannot automatically approve access before the gateway and Cloudflare Access policy are deployed, tested and authorized.
access.overviewIntro: These figures count entries in the published register, not the number of complaints, letters sent or requests received. No private record is available here.

access.sitewideIntro: Approved HTML pages remain directly accessible. Only cited source files (PDFs, office documents and external document providers) can trigger an access request. The lock identifies an approval request, not an existing technical restriction.
access.sitewideReference: Public reference of the requested document
access.sitewideInstructions: Include this reference, the page where you found it, your role and the purpose of the request when contacting us. This is not an official case reference and does not guarantee that a private copy exists.
access.sitewideWithoutReference: No specific reference was provided. Please identify the document title and the page where you found it when making contact.
access.sitewidePublicNotice: An access request grants no automatic right to the source. Already published files remain accessible at their existing URLs until separately removed or protected. Confidential originals require review, redaction and approval.
